text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.49% today as oil prices climbed again, with Brent crude hitting $113—its highest level since May—after reports that the U.S. is preparing military strikes against Iran following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's infrastructure. The U.S. has already pulled diplomats from Saudi Arabia, a signal that geopolitical tension in the Middle East is escalating and could disrupt oil supply. Higher crude prices directly boost the revenues and profit margins of major oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

This move fits into a broader two-week rally of 9%, driven by growing risk that regional conflict could tighten global oil supplies at a time when diesel shortages are already pushing prices up due to Ukraine's strikes on Russian production. The energy sector is being re-priced higher on the assumption that crude will stay elevated or climb further if U.S.-Iran tensions worsen.
